findings.text: In fm1-lab's test on an emulated FM-1 with the newer UC25HQ80 flash chip, it didn't save anything, and its code accepts only the original chip. On units with the newer chip, expect settings to be lost at power-off and later installs to be refused (which then needs a USB download-mode rescue). Not yet confirmed on a real unit. Units with the original chip aren't affected.

From the code alone: Checks for the original Puya flash chip only. On newer FM-1 units (UC25HQ80 flash) firmware like this has kept saves in RAM only and refused later installs, which then needs a USB download-mode rescue. Check the project's notes for newer-unit support before installing on a recent FM-1.
Does not pose as a keyboard, mouse or drive over USB.

brick.reason: Saves to flash on the original chip (189 writes) but never on the UC25HQ80: changes would be kept in RAM only and lost at power-off.
